title: Software
text:
Released tools from my research. Each is open source and accompanies a paper.

scEEMS
Single-cell Enhanced Expression Modifier Scores — a machine learning framework for predicting cell-type-resolved brain eQTLs, used to identify variants explaining Alzheimer’s disease heritability.
Code Paper


gruyere
Genome-wide Rare Variant EnRichment Evaluation — a rare-variant association test that leverages functional annotations, applied to Alzheimer disease (published in AJHG, 2025).
Code Paper


parmigiano
An empirical Bayes framework for burden and dispersion rare-variant association tests, used to prioritize rare variants associated with Alzheimer’s disease.
Code Paper


LDmat
Efficiently queryable compression of linkage disequilibrium matrices, released as a Python package on PyPI.
Code PyPI Paper

title: Chirag M. Lakhani
text:
I develop statistical and deep learning methods for predicting the functional effects of regulatory genetic variants, and apply them to understand cell-type-specific gene regulation in neurodegenerative disease. My current work integrates genomic deep learning models with functional genomics data to identify causal variants and uncover missing regulation in Alzheimer’s disease.
I am a Senior Research Scientist at the New York Genome Center, working with David Knowles (Columbia University/New York Genome Center) and Towfique Raj (Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai), and a member of the NIH Alzheimer’s Disease Sequencing Project consortium, where I collaborate with members of the AI/ML and Functional Genomics Working Group. My work is supported by the NIH/NIA-funded U01 AG068880, Learning the Regulatory Code of Alzheimer’s Disease Genomes, part of the ADSP Functional Genomics Consortium (FunGen-AD).
Trained in pure mathematics, I moved through computational topology and geometric data analysis into industry machine learning, then to biomedical data science at Harvard Medical School, before joining the Genome Center in 2021.
Contact: clakhani (at) nygenome.org

title: Chirag M. Lakhani
text:
Research Interests

Deep learning models of gene regulation and variant effect prediction
Rare variant gene discovery and common variant fine-mapping in Alzheimer’s disease
Discovery of cell-specific deep learning annotations which can be used as priors for fine-mapping and rare variant association testing
